label: Real run on this Mac's Docker Compose stack, with synthetic traffic from klaxon.traffic: synthetic data, a simulated provider, no real money. One fault from klaxon.faults, duplicate-delivery, was injected on purpose. The alert was raised by klaxon.alerts from what the stack showed. The harness withheld recent_deploys, service_health: each call to it got the error its source gives when it does not answer, and never reached that source (an outage simulated for this case; the stack itself was not touched). Klaxon's loop ran live on it, through Claude Code on Aravind's seat, and stopped on diagnosed after 12 steps; any reply it got is a recorded response, not a simulation. It was offered one write action (rollback_deploy), as in week 4; in an evaluation run its gate only plans an action the diagnosis names: nobody is asked, and nothing runs. The diagnosis was compared with the fault's recorded cause by a rule (klaxon.grading), not by a person or a model. Code planned the action its diagnosis named (redeploy ledger-consumer: LEDGER_HANDLER naive -> idempotent, LEDGER_BAD_EVENTS dead_letter (unchanged)); in an evaluation run nobody is asked, and nothing ran. The fault's cause was removed by the harness's clearing (klaxon.faults).

Rolling the ledger consumer back still fits the remedy: code plans a rollback from the deploy log, not from the tools.

diagnosis.hypothesis: ledger-consumer's duplicate check no longer stops a repeat of an event it has already booked. For evt_000281 ($157.18 charge, pay_000259) and evt_000368 ($18.25 refund, pay_000324), the provider sent the webhook a second time about 0.5 s after the receiver had acked the first with 200. The receiver published both copies. On each second copy the ledger ran a lookup (a DB span with empty query text), then inserted a new transaction (282, 370) and its entries. The first copy had been committed 0.5 s earlier and takes about 3 ms to process, so a race between the two copies is very unlikely. The check itself misses, through a wrong key, a changed handler or a broken lookup. transactions.event_id evidently has no unique constraint. The result is $157.18 overbooked on pay_000259 and $18.25 overrefunded on pay_000324, a net +$138.93. The alert's $157.18 came before the second duplicate (20:13:02), so the fault is still active. Not known: why the check broke, and whether a deploy caused it.

evidence.shows: Rerun at cutoff 20:13:03 still fails. evt_000281 is posted twice (txns 281, 282) and evt_000368 twice (txns 369, 370), net +$138.93. Per payment: pay_000259 ledger 23577 vs provider 7859, which fits a 15718 charge posted twice less a 7859 refund. pay_000324: ledger 0 vs provider 1825. The ledger balances, and our payment and refund records agree with the provider, so only the ledger is wrong.

webhook-receiver queued evt_000281 twice, at partition 1 offsets 120 (20:12:39.667) and 121 (20:12:40.172), with different trace ids. It does not dedupe, and the provider resent the event within 0.5 s.
ledger-consumer logged 'posted' for evt_000281 from both offset 120 and offset 121. The second copy was booked about 0.5 s after the first.

Second-copy trace: the receiver returned 200 'queued'. The ledger made a DB call with empty query text (likely the duplicate lookup), then ran INSERT transactions and INSERT entries, outcome 'posted', all within about 3 ms. payment-confirmer's guarded UPDATE gave 'already_confirmed', so that consumer is idempotent and the ledger is not.
evt_000368 has the same pattern: queued at offsets 152 and 153 (20:13:02.503 and 20:13:03.007), and posted by the ledger both times. This happened after the alert fired, so the fault is ongoing.

Over 2h the ledger shows 17 'already_processed' against about 636 'posted', so the check works sometimes, perhaps only before some change. The ~650 ledger outcomes exceed the ~370 event ids in c1; the cause is unclear (counter extrapolation or an earlier run), so this metric is only weak evidence. payment-confirmer's many already_confirmed may be API-side confirmation, not redelivery.

proposed_fix.summary: Roll ledger-consumer back to its settings before its latest deploy, in case a deploy (for example of LEDGER_HANDLER) broke the duplicate check. Deploy history could not be read (c2 and c7: Docker did not answer), and code will refuse the rollback if there is no such deploy. If it is refused, fix the check in code: dedupe on provider event_id and add a UNIQUE constraint on transactions.event_id, so a repeat insert fails and is treated as already_processed. In either case, a human must separately repair the books: reverse duplicate transactions 282 and 370 with compensating entries, then rerun the money check.

diagnosis.blast_radius: ledger-consumer's container is recreated, so ledger booking pauses briefly. Kafka keeps the messages and consumption resumes from the committed offset, but messages around the restart may be redelivered, which is the very case the check mishandles. If the old version has the same bug, nothing improves. The rollback repairs nothing: transactions 282 and 370 stay wrong until data repair. Other services are untouched.
diagnosis.rollback_plan: Redeploy ledger-consumer with the settings it had before the rollback, as recorded in the deploy log. Then confirm through posted/already_processed metrics and a money check rerun that it consumes normally.
